literal: Inside the drain spilled ambrosia it is like, one's own group-members those who are not in front of discourse holding.
translation: Holding a discourse before those who are not of one's own kind is like spilling ambrosia into a dirty drain.
modern: தமது தகுதியைப் போன்ற தகுதி இல்லாதவர்கள் முன்னே ஒரு பொருளைப் பற்றிப் பேசுவது, சாக்கடையில் சிந்திய அமிழ்தத்தைப் போன்றது.
explanation: The couplet warns against sharing valuable knowledge with an unreceptive or unsuited audience. 'கோட்டி கொளல்' means holding a discourse or sharing profound words. Doing this before people who are not of one's own kind ('தம் கணத்தார் அல்லார் முன்')—meaning those who lack the refinement or understanding to appreciate it—is a waste. The poet compares this to 'அமிழ்து' (ambrosia), the most precious and life-giving substance, being spilled into an 'அங்கணம்' (a dirty drain), where it is completely ruined and useless.
